title: Nvidia (NVDA) Plays Matchmaker to Drive Nordic AI Data Center Boom
excerpt: NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ:NVDA) has been introducing companies that hold its GPUs to data-center operators with available capacity in the Nordics, two sourc...
content_html:
Fatima Gulzar

Fri, August 28, 2026 at 11:34 AM EDT 4 min read

NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ:NVDA) has been introducing companies that hold its GPUs to data-center operators with available capacity in the Nordics, two sources familiar with the matter told CNBC. One source said Nvidia has proactively approached data-center companies to sound out potential offtakers, customers who commit to buying or leasing computing capacity, often without disclosing which company it is representing.

Nvidia CFO Colette Kress confirmed in June that the company has "certainly engaged" in matchmaking, asking "how can we help them obtain land, power, shell" and stand up compute "as fast as possible." A Savills report ranked Oslo, Stockholm, and Helsinki among the top six global locations for future data-center development, noting the region's abundant power and land.

Bull Case

NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ:NVDA) is extending its influence well beyond chip sales into the infrastructure that determines how fast its chips actually get deployed. Nvidia's reach now spans its software stack, government relationships, and direct investments in other companies, in addition to matchmaking. Controlling more of the ecosystem around its GPUs, not just the GPUs themselves, deepens customer dependence on Nvidia at every stage of building AI capacity.

Matchmaking solves the main problem slowing down Nvidia's sales: customers with chip orders but nowhere to deploy them. The value proposition is helping customers stand up the compute as fast as possible. It means faster deployment turns into faster revenue recognition on Nvidia's own GPU shipments and not just a favor to customers.

The Nordics specifically offer Nvidia a market with genuine structural tailwinds to break into. Savills' Rupert Duckworth said the region offers "one of the clearest delivery propositions globally" for AI-driven growth due to abundant power and land. Norway alone has more than 4 gigawatts of data-center capacity awaiting grid connection, according to the country's grid operator. Neoclouds and hyperscalers including Nebius and Microsoft have already signed deals there in 2026, giving Nvidia a fast-growing region to route its own customers into.

Bear Case

NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ:NVDA) is deepening its role as an intermediary in deals it does not fully control, which carries reputational exposure if a matched deal goes badly. Acting as an unofficial broker between GPU buyers and data-center operators, often without disclosing the parties involved. So Nvidia's name becomes attached to infrastructure outcomes, land, power, and construction timelines that ultimately depend on other companies executing well.
